lines.text: 0.9% saline: 0.9 g NaCl made up to 1 L
0.9% (w/v) = 0.9 g per 100 mL = 9.0 g per liter; 9.0 g / 58.44 g/mol = 0.154 mol; 0.154 M = 154 mM NaCl
0.9% saline: 0.9 g NaCl made up to 100 mL

objective: Calculate molarity and convert between grams, moles and millimoles for a simple solution such as 0.9 percent saline
secondaryObjectives: Apply tonicity to predict which way water moves when a cell sits in a hypertonic, isotonic or hypotonic solution, and what happens to the cell's volume
Explain how electrolytes (sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride) dissociate into ions in water and why their concentrations matter for nerve and muscle function

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch. 'Molarity is defined as the number of moles of solute in exactly 1 liter (1 L) of the solution', M = mol solute / L solution; when a mass is given, 'use the solute's molar mass to obtain the amount of solute in moles'. The 0.9 percent (weight per volume) convention, 9 g per liter, and NaCl's molar mass of 58.44 g/mol are the author's arithmetic.
Every organization, person, count and deadline is invented teaching data; tool output is an authored rendering in the tool style.

brief.situation: You are the student assistant in the physiology teaching lab at Whitmore Community College (fictional). Today's osmosis lab uses sheep red blood cells in three solutions; the control should be isotonic 0.9% saline. In yesterday's trial the cells in the control tube burst. The prep sheet is open. The lab starts at 10:00. It is 09:05. These solutions are for a teaching demonstration only.

parts.label: What was wrong
parts.criteria: 0.9% w/v means 0.9 g per 100 mL, so 9.0 g per liter; the sheet used 0.9 g per liter, 15.4 mM instead of 154 mM, a hypotonic solution, so water moved into the cells and they burst.

parts.label: What you changed
parts.criteria: 9.0 g NaCl made up to 1 L: 9.0 / 58.44 = 0.154 mol, 0.154 M; adding to 1 L of water changes the final volume; adding 0.1 g is still far too dilute.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: The arithmetic gives 154 mM and a trial tube keeps the cells' shape.

scoring.modelReasoning: Cells bursting in the control means it is hypotonic. 0.9% weight per volume is 0.9 g per 100 mL, so 9.0 g per liter; the sheet used 0.9 g per liter. In moles, 0.9 g / 58.44 g/mol = 0.0154 mol, a 15.4 mM solution, a tenth of the intended 154 mM, so water moved into the cells. Make 9.0 g NaCl up to 1 L (0.154 M), and confirm with a trial tube.
